verses.1: To the choirmaster. A masked psalm of the sons of Korah.
verses.2: Like a deer that pants for the streams of water, so my soul pants for you, O God.
verses.3: My soul is thirsty for the living God. When will I come and see the face of God?
verses.4: My tears have become my food day and night, while they say to me every day, “Where is your God?”
verses.5: These things I remember, and I pour out my soul: how I would go through the desolate place and come to the house of God, with a voice of joy and praise, among the voices of those who are celebrating.
verses.6: Why are you downcast, O my soul? And why do you groan within me? Hope in God, for I will still praise Him, the salvation of my face and my God.
verses.7: My soul is troubled within me; therefore I will remember You from the land of Jordan and from Hermon, from Mount Mizar.
verses.8: Deep calls to deep at the sound of Your waterfalls; all Your waves and breakers have gone over me.
verses.9: By day the Lord will complete His steadfast love, and at night His song will be with me—a prayer to the God of my life.
verses.10: I say to God, my rock, “Why have You forgotten me? Why must I walk in gloom, oppressed by my enemy?”
verses.11: My enemies, in their pride, have crushed me; all day they say to me, “Where is your God?”
verses.12: Why are you downcast, O my soul? And why do you groan within me? Hope in God, for I will still praise Him, the salvation of my face and my God.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "A masked psalm" (maskil) is a traditional rendering for מַשְׂכִּיל, indicating a reflective or instructive psalm.
- v. 5: “Come to the house of God” reflects the poetic structure and intent of the Hebrew, which uses metaphor to express longing for worship and divine presence.
- v. 7: “Mount Mizar” is a possible variant or poetic reference; the Hebrew term מִצְעָר is uncertain, but “Mount Mizar” is a plausible interpretation.
- v. 8: “Deep calls to deep” captures the poetic parallelism in תְּהוֹם־אֶל־תְּהוֹם. The reference to waterfalls and waves enhances the imagery of overwhelming emotion.
